one_month_reasoning: The main event in the window is Q3 2026 results on 2026-10-29 (call 10:00 AM), three days before the 1-month date. Industry read-across going in is positive: Amphenol guided another mid-teens sequential rise in IT datacom for Q3, Lam called the 2027 WFE setup 'extraordinary', and the FY27 budget request lifts missile procurement by 188%. So a beat or a guidance raise is more likely than a miss. Against that, the stock is at its 52-week high ($312 vs $314.24), up about 30% since the August beat, and trades at roughly the consensus target (~$304-307). A beat looks mostly priced in, and a sell-the-news reaction or a narrow beat could easily give back 10% or more. I see the two sides as offsetting, so I centred the distribution on today's price (median about $312) with a monthly sigma of about 16.5%. That is close to the stock's realized 59%/3.5, with a little extra for the earnings print.

fair_value.method: Blend of 32x forward P/E on 2028E EPS of $10.00, which the market will treat as NTM by Oct-2027 ($320, 60% weight), and 20x EV/EBITDA on 2028E adj. EBITDA of $370M less ~$0.40B net debt over 21.1M shares ($333, 40% weight). Result: about $325.

inputs_detail.derivation: Backlog was up about 30% YoY at end of Q2 and every segment grew sales by double digits. Demand down the chain is accelerating: WFE is guided to ~$209.5B in 2027 from low-$150B in 2026, Amphenol IT datacom is +63% organic, and missile procurement in the FY27 request is +188%. I take a mid-teens value-added sales growth rate, continuing 2026, plus modest margin leverage, which gives low-20s EPS growth. That is below the +30% of 2026 because 2026 benefited from Electronic Materials margin recovery (23%->32%) that will not repeat at the same rate.

New capacity comes online: the Elmore beryllium expansion funded by a defense prime, and JX's sputter-target capacity +60% in H2 FY2027, which signals target demand growth industry-wide. I fade growth toward mid-teens because semis and defense are cyclical.

Carpenter Technology, the closest high-quality US aerospace and specialty-alloy peer, trades at ~32.6x forward. Today MTRN is ~44.6x 2026E and ~36x my 2027E. I assume it de-rates to the peer forward multiple as growth normalises from +30% toward mid-teens.

methods.name: EV/EBITDA
methods.inputs: 2028E adj. EBITDA $370M x 20x = EV $7.40B; less net debt ~$0.40B = equity $7.0B / 21.1M shares = ~$333

inputs_detail.derivation: Q2 annualised is ~$287M for 2026. I grow it ~15% in 2027 (~$330M) and ~12% in 2028 (~$370M), in line with the backlog and downstream demand assumptions used for EPS.
Debt $440.7M less cash $20.0M. H1 FCF was $39M and is roughly offset by capex and the dividend, so I assume only modest paydown.
Equivalent to the ~32x peer P/E after adjusting for MTRN's D&A and interest load. The current EV of ~$7.0B on ~$287M run-rate EBITDA is ~24x, and I assume partial de-rating.

bear.story: The AI and semis capex cycle peaks in 2027 (an HBM digestion phase) and Electronic Materials margins fall back from 32% toward the mid-20s. Defense ramps slip because Congress does not fund the reconciliation share of missile procurement. EPS stalls near $7.5 and the multiple compresses to ~25x, comparable to the stock's pre-2026 history.

base.story: Backlog converts and 2027 EPS reaches ~$8.6. The Street rolls forward to 2028E of ~$10 at a ~32-33x peer multiple. The stock grinds sideways to modestly up after a 155% run.

bull.story: WFE reaches ~$210B in 2027, Amphenol-style AI datacom demand pulls beryllium-nickel and clad strip, and missile funding is enacted at the 188% increase. The Elmore capacity is sold out, EPS beats to $11+ by 2028E and the stock holds a ~42x premium scarcity multiple as the sole Western integrated beryllium producer.

thesis_break_reason: Below ~$205 (about 34% below today, roughly one year-sigma down), the market would be pricing EPS back near 2025 levels times a historical ~28x multiple. That would most likely mean a fundamental break rather than noise: a reversal in backlog (book-to-bill well below 1), Electronic Materials margins collapsing as semis capex turns, or defense budget funding for munitions failing. The level is also below where the stock traded before the August beat and raise.

key_uncertainties: Durability of the AI/semis capex cycle into 2028 versus a digestion phase that would hit Electronic Materials (32% EBITDA margin in Q2)
Whether Congress funds the reconciliation portion (~55%) of FY27 missile procurement on schedule
Multiple sustainability: at ~45x 2026E the stock embeds a scarcity premium, and the consensus target (~$304-307) sits at the price
Beryllium supply-chain shifts (Kazakhstan's Ulba processing Rwandan ore) and competitor capacity additions in sputter targets (JX +60%)
Realized vol of 59% and a 155% one-year move raise reversal risk
reasoning: Company facts: Q2 2026 was a record quarter, with adj. EPS of $1.90 (vs ~$1.52 expected), value-added sales up ~15% and adj. EBITDA margin 23.3%. Backlog was up ~30% YoY and FY26 EPS guidance was raised to $6.80-7.20. Net debt is ~$420M and diluted shares 21.1M. My lane is the value chain, which is uniformly strong. On semis, Lam calls the 2027 WFE setup 'extraordinary', industry forecasts put WFE at ~$209.5B in 2027, and JX Advanced Metals (~60% target share) grew target sales ~20% and is adding 60% capacity. On AI and data centres, Amphenol IT datacom is +63% organic and guided up again for Q3. On defense, the FY27 request includes a +188% missile procurement increase and a defense prime is funding $65M of Elmore beryllium capacity. On supply, the beryllium market is an oligopoly in which MTRN is the dominant Western integrated producer. IBC is exiting cast Be-Al, so there is less competition there, and Kazakhstan's Ulba is the main alternative supplier. All of this supports 20%+ EPS growth in 2027. However, the stock has already gone up ~2.5x and sits at the ~$304-307 consensus target and at ~45x 2026E, versus Carpenter at ~32.6x forward. My fair value of ~$325 implies only modest upside, because the growth I see is roughly offset by multiple de-rating. For the distribution, I put the median near $318 (fair value minus some de-rating risk) and used a lognormal sigma of ~0.47. That is below the 59% realized vol, which was inflated by the re-rating, and above a typical large-cap's 25-35%, given the cyclical semis and defense exposure and the small-cap float. The scenario mean (~$328) is consistent with this. Research used ~16 web queries and fetches. USGS MCS 2026 beryllium data could not be parsed (PDF tooling unavailable), and Twelve Data analyst endpoints were plan-restricted, so the consensus came from stockanalysis.com and press.
